alignments.note: English *told Jezebel* takes the addressee as a bare object, leaving the לְ unrendered.
The second כָּל is rendered by *withal* rather than repeating *all*; reading *withal* as an addition and כָּל as unrepresented is also defensible.

The MT oath formula here has no indirect object, so *to me* answers to no Hebrew morpheme; per the chapter's convention for unlicensed English it is marked added rather than folded into יַעֲשׂוּן.
The second כֹה of the oath formula is carried by *also* while יוֹסִפוּן supplies *more*.
The oath particle כִּי is asseverative, and the ASV renders it with the discontinuous English self-imprecation *if … not*; there is no negative morpheme in the Hebrew.
*by* is the preposition the adverbial accusative licenses, and *to morrow* is the ASV's hyphenated spelling tokenized in two.
כְּנֶפֶשׁ carries no article; the ASV's *the* is supplied and stays with the noun.
The Hebrew verb has no object; the ASV's subordinating *when* and resumptive object *that* are both supplied by the narrative construction and stay with the verb.
The waw of the apodosis is absorbed by the English *when* clause.
The destination is an adverbial accusative, so the supplied *to* belongs to the place name.
The verbless possessive clause supplies *belongeth*; the לְ itself is *to*.
The independent pronoun is emphatic beside an inflected verb, which the ASV renders *he himself*.

The ASV renders the construct attributively with the English possessive *a day's*. The supplied *a* determines *day* — a journey of one day — not *journey*, exactly as *the* in *the king's son* determines *king*.
*tree* is the ASV's specifier; רֹתֶם itself is the shrub named *juniper*.
אֶחָד here is the indefinitizing numeral, which the ASV renders as the article *a*.
נַפְשׁוֹ is rendered by the single reflexive *himself*, so noun and suffix share one unit; *for* is the preposition the English verb licenses.
The לְ of the purpose infinitive is carried by the complementizer *that*.
The verbless clause supplies *am*, and the comparative טוֹב מִן is rendered *better*.

variant_decisions.evidence: Qere אֶחָ֑ד (HAcmsa) and ketiv אחת (HAcfsa) are the same numeral lemma 259 differing only in gender agreement with masculine רֹתֶם. ASV "sat down under a juniper-tree" renders the numeral as the indefinite article either way, so neither reading leaves a trace in the English and no note is mapped here.
